meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid (English common law and French civil law as received at independence in 1980, with customary law recognized as a formal source of law under Article 47 of the Constitution of the Republic of Vanuatu)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Vanuatu–Australia Bilateral Investment Treaty (signed 1988, in force)
Vanuatu–United Kingdom Investment Promotion and Protection Agreement (in force)
Vanuatu–France Agreement on the Encouragement and Protection of Investments (in force)
Vanuatu–People's Republic of China Bilateral Investment Treaty (signed 2004, in force)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Vanuatu AML/CFT and UBO obligations are governed by: (i) the Anti-Money Laundering and Terrorism Financing Act No. 23 of 2016, as amended, which defines a 'beneficial owner' as any natural person who ultimately owns or controls 25% or more of the shares, voting rights, or ownership interest, or who otherwise exercises control over the legal person; (ii) the International Companies Act No. 32 of 1992 [Cap 222], as amended, which requires every International Company to maintain a VFSC-licensed registered agent and registered office in Vanuatu and to keep accurate registers of directors, shareholders, and beneficial owners; (iii) the Companies Act [Cap 191]; (iv) the Vanuatu Financial Services Commission Act No. 10 of 2016; and (v) directives and guidance issued by the Vanuatu Financial Services Commission ('VFSC') and the Vanuatu Financial Intelligence Unit ('VFIU'). The AML/TF Act imposes mandatory customer due diligence, beneficial-ownership verification, suspicious-transaction reporting, and record-retention duties on licensed agents and reporting entities; failure to identify a natural-person UBO is a mandatory ground for refusal of the client relationship.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of the valid passport of each director, shareholder, and ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National passport authority of the UBO's or director's country of origin, with certification by a licensed notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille under the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention where the state of origin is a contracting party; otherwise Vanuatu consular legalization at the competent Vanuatu diplomatic mission

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address (utility bill or bank statement issued within the last three months)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Public utility provider or regulated financial institution in the UBO's or director's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized attestation of authenticity, followed by Hague Apostille or Vanuatu consular legalization where the document is a public document

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter introducing the client and confirming banking relationship and general source of funds
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed depository bank in the UBO's country of origin or the correspondent bank servicing the transaction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization with witnessed signature and, where required, Hague Apostille or Vanuatu consular legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Police clearance certificate / criminal record certificate for each director and ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National police or criminal records authority of each country of ordinary residence during the preceding five years
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille where the issuing state is an Apostille Convention member; otherwise Vanuatu consular legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incorporation, constitutional documents, and certificate of good standing for any corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate registry of the ultimate parent entity's country of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Vanuatu consular legalization as applicable, with certification of any English or French translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized source-of-wealth declaration, curriculum vitae, and professional business reference for each UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: The UBO or director executing before a notary public, with the professional reference issued by the UBO's bank, legal counsel, or accountant
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization plus Hague Apostille or Vanuatu consular legalization when the declaration is executed in a foreign jurisdiction

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of every director, shareholder, UBO, and authorized signatory against: (i) the United Nations Consolidated Sanctions List; (ii) the U.S. OFAC Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) and non-SDN sanctions lists; (iii) the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List; (iv) the UK HM Treasury consolidated sanctions list; and (v) the Vanuatu domestic list of designated persons and politically exposed persons (PEPs) maintained by the Vanuatu Financial Intelligence Unit. Screening must include reverse PEP matching for immediate family members and close associates, must be refreshed within 24 hours of any appointment or ownership change and at least quarterly thereafter, and must be documented in an audit trail retained for at least five years after termination of the business relationship. Enhanced due diligence, independent corroboration of source of funds, and senior-management approval are compulsory for any PEP match or for funds sourced from jurisdictions on the FATF list of high-risk and monitored jurisdictions.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC) — 'VFSC Online Services' company name search and reservation portal (official website: https://www.vfsc.vu; Corporate Registry division)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be filed in Latin (Roman) script. The official languages of Vanuatu are Bislama, English, and French, and all three are accepted for naming; names originating in non-Latin scripts such as Cyrillic, CJK, Arabic, or Greek must be transliterated into Latin characters, and the transliteration must be unique, pronounceable, and consistent across all statutory documents. The certificate of incorporation records only the Latin-script version. An International Company must bear an acceptable legal-form suffix such as 'Limited', 'Ltd', 'Corporation', 'Corp', 'Incorporated', 'Inc', 'Société Anonyme', or 'S.A.'. The VFSC automatically rejects names that are identical, misleadingly similar, or confusingly similar to an existing registered name, a reserved name, or a protected mark.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within 14 calendar days of receiving a name-rejection notice from the VFSC Registry, the applicant or its licensed registered agent may: (1) resubmit up to three alternative proposed names through the VFSC Online Services portal, paying the applicable re-search fee; (2) file a written reconsideration request addressed to the Registrar of International Companies, annexing legal submissions and any ministerial consent already obtained for a sensitive token; (3) if reconsideration is refused, lodge an internal administrative appeal to the VFSC Board within 30 days of the refusal under the VFSC Act review framework; and (4) as the final administrative remedy, apply for judicial review before the Supreme Court of Vanuatu under the Civil Procedure Rules on grounds of procedural irregularity or error of law. The name-clearance certificate must be issued before the incorporation application is submitted, and no lawful incorporation may precede a positive clearance decision.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Acceptable. An International Company operating a remote video-matching and cross-border social telephony business may satisfy its statutory registered-office obligation solely through the premises of a VFSC-licensed registered agent in Vanuatu; no employees, equipment, or servers need be located at the registered address. Shared-office, virtual-office, and professional-mailbox configurations are therefore permissible at the pre-incorporation stage, provided the registered agent maintains custody of the statutory registers, UBO records, and service-of-process facilities. This arrangement does not, by itself, satisfy any future economic-substance or licensing test if the company later applies for a VFSC financial or securities dealing licence.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk: Low-to-Moderate. For a dormant or low-volume International Company held through a compliant licensed agent, the estimated annual probability of an unannounced VFSC or VFIU on-site inspection touching the company's records is 15-25%. The probability rises above 60% per annum if: (i) the video-matching platform's payment rails (Apple IAP and Paymentwall) generate high-risk cross-border transaction patterns; (ii) a foreign financial intelligence unit issues a request for information or mutual legal assistance; or (iii) the VFSC conducts a targeted beneficial-ownership compliance sweep. Upon inspection, the registered agent must produce the UBO register, client due-diligence files, and statutory records within the statutory production window.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: International Companies Act 1992 (No. 32 of 1992), as amended; ss. 6-9 (Incorporation), s. 10 (Registered Agent), s. 14 (Registered Office), ss. 26-29 (Share Capital and Shares).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC), International Companies Registry, Port Vila, Vanuatu, in conjunction with a licensed registered agent.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Memorandum and Articles of Association filed with VFSC Form IC-1 (Incorporation Application), resulting in issuance of the Certificate of Incorporation.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; no escrow account required. Subscriber shares may be issued for nominal or no consideration in any currency. The US$250 state filing fee is payable to VFSC but does not constitute paid-up capital.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: By voting consent of all directors: 1. The Memorandum and Articles of Association as submitted to VFSC are adopted and approved in their final form. 2. The subscriber's application for 1 ordinary share at US$1.00 par value is ratified, and share certificate no. 1 is issued to the subscriber. 3. The registered office shall be maintained at the Vanuatu address of YZ Corporate Services Ltd, the first registered agent. 4. The following officers are appointed: [Name], Director and Chief Executive Officer; [Name], Director; [Name], Company Secretary. 5. The officers are authorized to execute filings with VFSC and to open any bank or payment accounts required for the app's commercial operations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC), International Companies Registry, via registered agent portal.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit two (2) proposed names (primary and alternate) to VFSC through the licensed registered agent. Pay the search and reservation fee. Wait for VFSC confirmation that the proposed names do not conflict with an existing company, reserved name, or prohibited statutory word.
required_dossiers: Corporate search evidence for both names
Proof of name reservation fee payment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If primary name is refused, the agent automatically submits the alternate name. If both names are refused, the founder resubmits with three new distinct names within 3 business days without re-notarization.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution and Submission of Incorporation Application
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: VFSC, International Companies Registry, Port Vila.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The registered agent lodges Form IC-1, together with the Memorandum and Articles of Association, declaration that the IC will not carry on business with Vanuatu residents, and audited/declared consent forms for first directors, secretary, and shareholder. The application is submitted electronically and physically.
required_dossiers: Consent to act as director and/or secretary
Founder/subscriber identification and proof of address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If VFSC queries any inconsistency, the registered agent files a formal amendment or supplementary declaration within 5 business days. If defects relate to non-compliant articles, resubmit corrected Memorandum and Articles with no additional penalty if done within the statutory cure window.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Payment of Official VFSC Filing Fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: VFSC Treasury and Payments Unit, Port Vila, Vanuatu.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon invoice from VFSC, the registered agent pays the US$250 state incorporation fee plus any agency disbursement fees by bank transfer or VFSC-approved electronic payment. Payment reference number is recorded against the application file.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If payment is misapplied, present bank swift/MT103 evidence and request payment reallocation; VFSC processes within 2 business days and continues the incorporation review.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation and Statutory Registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: VFSC, International Companies Registry, Port Vila.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: VFSC verifies the application, issues the Certificate of Incorporation, and opens the company's public registry record. The registered agent receives the certificate and prepares the company's statutory registers (register of members, directors, secretaries, and charges).
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate contains typographical errors, the registered agent files a rectification request with the certificate original and a correction affidavit; VFSC reissues corrected certificate within 2 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Governance and Registered Agent Compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registered agent YZ Corporate Services Ltd, Port Vila, Vanuatu; VFSC as supervisory registry.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The registered agent maintains the registered office and the statutory registers at its Vanuatu address. The first board resolution and consent actions are executed, and the agent files any required notification of registered address or officer changes with VFSC within the statutory period.
required_dossiers: Register of members and share certificates
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If VFSC requires an updated director or address notification, the agent files Form IC-8 with updated consents within 5 business days to maintain good standing.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: None — pure digital service with no manufacturing, warehouse, or industrial facility in Vanuatu.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: None — International Company conducting business wholly outside Vanuatu is exempt from the Vanuatu Business Licence under the Business Licence Act [Cap. 244]; no special telecom or gambling licence is required for a non-gambling real-time video chat/social telephony application.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Vanuatu Department of Environmental Protection and Conservation (DEPC)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — no physical project works, no land modification, no infrastructure, and no material resource use subject to the Environmental Impact Assessment provisions of the Environmental Protection and Conservation Act [Cap. 283].
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable — zero point-source wastewater, VOC, or solid waste emissions generated in Vanuatu. Any electronic waste originating from servers or devices is handled by the cloud hosting provider under its data centre's environmental compliance programme. If a Vanuatu physical office is later opened, DEPC waste disposal and sanitation standards would apply.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not applicable — no physical premises, plant, or assembly occupancy in Vanuatu; therefore no fire safety certificate, structural load inspection, or workplace safety clearance is currently required. Employees operate remotely. If a Vanuatu office is established, the National Fire Service and Department of Labour clearance will become mandatory under the Fire Service Act and Health and Safety at Work Act.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Vanuatu Revenue and Customs Administration (VRCA), Ministry of Finance and Economic Management, Republic of Vanuatu; International Company (IC) statutory registration is administered by the Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC). Tax e-portals: VRCA VAT e-filing and ASYCUDA World customs clearance, accessible via the national Government portal at www.gov.vu.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned Vanuatu International Company is first incorporated with the VFSC, obtaining a VFSC Registry Number and Certificate of Incorporation. If the IC makes taxable supplies in Vanuatu or imports commercial goods, the foreign entity must file VAT Form 1 (Application for Registration) with VRCA together with certified constitutional documents, proof of physical address, and officer/shareholder particulars; VRCA issues a unique 8-digit VAT identification number endorsed on the VAT registration certificate, typically within 10 business days after verification. For customs transactions, a trader code is obtained electronically through ASYCUDA World upon presentation of the VAT certificate and, where onshore activity exists, a valid Business Licence. Where the IC conducts wholly offshore business, no local business licence or VAT ID is required; a VFSC Registry tax-status letter is used to evidence statutory exemption.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Vanuatu levies no income, capital gains, withholding, or stamp tax, so no check-the-box or hybrid-mismatch elections exist under local law. Available elections include: (1) voluntary VAT registration and group VAT registration under Sections 8-10 of the Value Added Tax Act [CAP 250], allowing input tax recovery; (2) reclassification election under Sections 14-15 of the International Companies Act [CAP 222] to convert an IC into a domestic company, or vice versa, with VFSC and Ministerial consent; (3) redomiciliation election enabling a foreign-incorporated company to transfer its registration into the VFSC registry as an International Company; and (4) election to apply zero-rating to qualifying export contracts by submitting a written export-determination schedule at the time of supply.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) under the Value Added Tax Act [CAP 250], administered by VRCA; separate customs import duties apply under the Customs Act to goods imported into Vanuatu.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Mandatory registration is triggered where taxable turnover exceeds VT 4,000,000 (approximately USD 33,000) in any rolling 12-month period; voluntary registration is permitted below that threshold. Non-resident suppliers of remote and digital services are within the Vanuatu VAT net only where the supply is made for the direct benefit of a person in Vanuatu, and registration is required if the same VT 4,000,000 threshold is met through Vanuatu-sourced supplies; no separate low-value digital-services registration threshold currently exists.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, tax-authority API validation, or digital stamping regime is currently in force. VAT-registered persons must issue an original tax invoice within 28 days of supply for all taxable supplies exceeding VT 1,000, showing sequential numbering, the VAT registration number, a description of the supply, and the 12.5% tax split; invoices may be manual, printed, or generated through the taxpayer's own ERP system. Customs export and import declarations, however, are cleared in real time through ASYCUDA World, which requires electronic lodgement and digital risk-based validation before goods are released.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A registered person may apply 0% VAT to: (a) goods physically exported from Vanuatu under a customs export declaration, ordinarily removed within 30 days of supply or within a 60-day extended period approved by VRCA; (b) services supplied for the direct and sole benefit of a non-resident recipient located outside Vanuatu, including cross-border social-telephony and video-matching platform services where no consumer in Vanuatu receives the benefit; and (c) supplies to exempt international organisations. The zero-rating claim requires contemporaneous evidence that the goods left Vanuatu or that the service benefit was received offshore, retained in the taxpayer's VAT working file.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SAD) and VRCA/ASYCUDA clearance endorsement evidencing physical export from Vanuatu
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing shipment to a foreign destination with the consignee located outside Vanuatu
Inward Remittance Certificate or foreign-currency credit advice from a licensed Vanuatu bank evidencing receipt of export proceeds from overseas
Commercial invoice and packing list matching the customs declaration particulars
Executed export-services contract, platform usage report for the offshore jurisdiction, and non-resident customer attestation for zero-rated services
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: VRCA may audit zero-rated export supplies within the 5-year statutory assessment window, extended to 7 years where returns were not filed; exporters must produce the full documentary bundle, including bank credit evidence and customs departure records. Misdeclared or fraudulent zero-rating entails the following: additional tax of up to 25% of the short-paid VAT for careless errors, rising to 100% for intentional evasion; statutory interest on refunded or clawed-back amounts; cancellation or retrospective de-registration with recovery of all previously refunded input VAT as a debt due; and criminal liability for tax fraud under Section 65 of the VAT Act, carrying a fine of up to VT 10,000,000 and/or imprisonment for up to 5 years. Additionally, VFSC may strike off or impose monetary penalties on an International Company for false declarations, without prejudice to money-laundering charges under the Financial Transactions Reporting Act.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Reserve Bank of Vanuatu (RBV) as the central monetary and exchange-control authority, acting under the Exchange Control Act [Cap 61] and the Financial Institutions Act; the Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC) regulates International Companies separately for corporate registry and AML/CFT purposes.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Vanuatu's currency, the vatu (VUV), is fully convertible for current-account purposes; Vanuatu is an IMF Article VIII-member jurisdiction and maintains no material exchange restrictions on resident current payments. Capital-account transfers for residents require RBV-approved dealer filings. International Companies are statutorily non-resident and fall outside the resident exchange-control perimeter, meaning inward equity contributions, trade payments, and profit remittances can circulate freely in VUV or foreign-currency accounts without RBV pre-approval, provided the company remains non-resident and does not transact with Vanuatu residents in vatu.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Resident exporters are obliged to surrender export proceeds through an RBV-Authorized Dealer within 21 days of receipt, with a mandatory conversion ratio of 100% into VUV (subject to RBV sector waivers). Non-resident International Companies are exempt from the surrender regime; however, commercial banks will require a sworn declaration of non-residency and the underlying commercial invoices to prevent the surrender obligation from being mechanically applied to operating inflows.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Bank of South Pacific (BSP) Vanuatu Limited

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low feasibility rating. Global Tier-1 digital EMIs (Wise, Payoneer, Airwallex, Currencycloud, Stripe Treasury) systematically decline VU-registered International Companies due to the residual FATF/EU AML risk memory of Vanuatu and the cross-border social-telephony product profile. Vanuatu has no domestically recognized EMI license class, so offshore EMIs can only be used as settlement wallets rather than as primary clearing accounts; a compliant structure is a BSP/ANZ operational bank account feeding a USD settlement wallet provided by a UK/EEA EMI licensed in a FATF-compliant state, with clear segregation of client funds and no crypto on/off ramps.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: BSP Vanuatu requires an in-person KYC interview of at least one director and the ultimate beneficial owner at a Port Vila or Luganville branch before activating a foreign-currency operational account; remote opening is not granted unless a VFSC-licensed registered agent certifies the principals and a live video KYC interview is recorded and retained. ANZ permits a hybrid model: remote file review, followed by a physical director visit within 12 months and a local fiduciary confirmation. NBV is door-opening only with unlimited in-person documentation. The recommended path is a Port Vila fiduciary introduction to BSP with certified corporate registry extracts and sworn non-residency declarations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: open-camera real-time video matching with App Store monetization and gift-charging is classified by banks as an intimacy/impersonation-adjacent digital sector, triggering enhanced due diligence and potential romance-scam facilitation risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Functional product demo and App Store listing; written Trust and Safety policy incorporating AI moderation, user identity verification, and prohibited-conduct rules; a bespoke AML/CFT business risk assessment aligned with FATF Recommendations 15 and 16; evidence of age-gating and territorial compliance; board-approved compliance manual; third-party overseas audit opinion of the moderation stack; and a transparent revenue model disclosure for Apple IAP and Paymentwall flows.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: historical bearer-share issuance risk for Vanuatu International Companies and uncertainty on the current shareholder register.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified full chronological shareholder register evidencing zero bearer instruments; original incorporation and amalgamation documents; VFSC Certificate of Good Standing; notarized sworn statement by the beneficial owners confirming chain of title; and a sanctions/negative-news screen (Dow Jones or Refinitiv) for every director, shareholder, and signatory.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: incoming funding volatility and opaque remittance chain because Apple distributes payouts from an Irish affiliate while Paymentwall consolidates multi-country collections, causing reconciliation mismatches.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed merchant agreements with Apple and Paymentwall; six-month payout ledger with bank statement cross-matching; a documented transaction-monitoring sampling methodology; evidence of client-money segregation and an escrow policy where applicable; and copies of any suspicious transaction reports filed to the VFSC or other competent authorities.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: substance deficiency of an International Company with no material office, staff, or local economic activity, potentially triggering shell-company classification.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: VFSC registered-agent certificate and service agreement; physical office or co-working lease; appointment of local resident director or compliance officer; board meeting minutes evidencing genuine management decisions; accounting/transfer-pricing documentation; RBV non-residency declaration; and a substance calendar proving the core business functions are performed from Vanuatu or a disclosed contractual offshore location.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Equity injection must be driven by an MT103 SWIFT wire from the ultimate parent or investor to a VUV/USD-denominated corporate account at BSP/ANZ in Port Vila with beneficiary field referencing the VFSC registration number, and SWIFT field 77B stating purpose code EQUI (equity injection). The instructing bank must transmit the board resolution authorizing the capital increase, a source-of-funds questionnaire, and the latest audited or management financials; the receiving bank then applies standard verification against the VFSC registry certificate and the non-residency declaration before crediting. Cash-pooling and intercompany recharge flows should be contractually documented and routed through the US correspondent network of the Vanuatu bank to avoid fragmented forensic trails.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For trade settlements and vendor payments, use SWIFT MT103 with clear invoice reference, BOP purpose code 3000 (goods) or 6700 (services), and pre-agreed beneficiary bank details to minimize correspondent holds. Large one-off settlements should be structured through a commercial letter of credit using swift MT700 (issue), MT707 (amendment), and MT799 (pre-advice), with Vanuatu-issued LCs advised through ANZ's and BSP's Australian/US clearing corridors. Dividend repatriation and profit remittance must follow the same MT103 rail with supporting board minutes and a tax-exemption certificate from the VFSC. For app-store and payment-gateway churn, weekly consolidated withdrawals from Apple IAP/Paymentwall to the operational account should be initiated to a single master wallet, then concentrated via MT103 to the company's treasury account.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore spot VUV/USD and VUV/EUR trades executed through RBV-authorized dealers (BSP, ANZ, BRED) for operational vatu balances and local disbursements
Offshore USD/VUV non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) booked through financial institutions in Singapore or Hong Kong, as no deep onshore deliverable forward market exists in Vanuatu
Offshore non-deliverable currency swaps (USD fixed vs VUV reference) between non-resident counterparties, with net settlement in USD, permitted provided no Vanuatu resident is a counterparty
Cross-currency interest-rate swaps and plain-vanilla FX options referencing the RBV mid-rate where the VUV leg is not delivered onshore

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before the anniversary of incorporation date; VFSC accepts up to 30 days after the anniversary only with late fee
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment fee of 10% of annual fee after 30 days; continued non-payment triggers notice of default and administrative strike-off within 90 days unless rectified

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC) via registered agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on the anniversary of incorporation; also within 14 days after any change in beneficial ownership
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines up to VT 1,000,000 (approx. USD 9,000) per false or late filing; directors and officers personally liable; administrative strike-off for continued default

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Registered Agent and Registered Office Continuation Declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC) through licensed registered agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filed concurrently with annual fee renewal on the anniversary of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to maintain registered agent/office constitutes a contravention of the International Companies Act; subject to penalty notice and potential strike-off

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Economic Substance Notification (if carrying on geographically mobile services)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually within 12 months from the end of the financial year, with notification return filed through the registered agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing incurs penalty of VT 500,000 (approx. USD 4,500); continued failure may result in compulsory strike-off and director disqualification

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No compulsory statutory audit for a Vanuatu International Company unless the company's constitution voluntarily requires an auditor appointment or the company becomes a licensed financial institution.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Vanuatu International Companies are exempt from local accounting filing; if financial statements are voluntarily prepared, the framework may be IFRS or a simple receipts-and-payments basis.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The International Company must maintain a beneficial ownership register and submit an annual confirmation to the VFSC through the registered agent. Any shareholding transfer or change in beneficial ownership exceeding 25% must be recorded and reported to the VFSC within 14 days of the change. The annual confirmation must reflect the current shareholding as of the anniversary date.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members, Register of Directors, Minute Book

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,500 – USD 7,000 per year (voluntary, if engaged)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0.00% -- Vanuatu imposes no national corporate income tax; no CIT statute is in force. The International Company (IC) under the International Companies Act 1992 (Cap 222) is statutorily exempt from Vanuatu income tax, capital gains tax and dividend tax.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: 0.00% effective rate on foreign-source profits of the IC. The IC Act exemption covers all Vanuatu taxes, duties and levies except the annual VFSC Government Maintenance Fee. VAT at 12.5% arises only on Vanuatu domestic supplies; digital video-match subscriptions sold to non-residents through Apple IAP and Paymentwall are zero-rated exports of services.
